name: badge
description: A small label that states who did something or what state it is in. Tone is spoken as text, never colour alone.

use.when: one word says a state, or who did something, beside the thing it describes.
use.not: as a button, a link, or decoration; never inside or right beside a link or button, where it looks like part of it; never a verb such as Publish, which reads as something to press.
use.with: card and event, where the state belongs to an item.

label.description: Short text such as 'Assistant' or 'Draft'. Say only what is not already obvious; a badge is not a place for timestamps.

tone.description: human, assistant, and system are provenance tones; the rest are states.

context.description: Words read after the label but not shown, when the label alone says nothing heard out of place: 'priority' after 'High'.

wcag.notes: 7:1 text on the tinted background in both themes. Meaning is carried by the label text, so the tone is decoration for sighted readers and data for machines.

machine.identify: Read data-tone for the category and data-actor when the badge states provenance (human, assistant, system). The text is the label.
